_what: How a player lead becomes a person.
_ruled: Ryan, 2026-09-08: if a man qualifies under the standing rule he IS promoted. No batch approval. The rule has already answered, and making him approve each batch turns a rule into a queue -- and the queue only grows as documents come in.
_the_rule: A person is someone who PLAYED, COACHED OR OFFICIATED at least one season. A player named on a ROSTER for a club-season the archive HOLDS qualifies. So does a man named in the caption to a TEAM PHOTOGRAPH, under the conditions in `_team_photograph_ruling` -- and under those conditions only.
_what_still_comes_to_ryan: What the rule REFUSES or flags as AMBIGUOUS. A man named only in a transaction or a camp list; a lead whose evidence kind the route does not know; and a name more than one held person carries. Those are judgements the rule cannot make and they are reported, never promoted. A team photograph WAS on this list until 2026-09-08 and is now ruled -- see `_team_photograph_ruling`.
_no_scope_key: There was an in_scope_stores / in_scope_club_seasons pair here and it is deliberately gone. A scope key is how a standing rule quietly becomes a queue again.
_refuse_by_default: An evidence kind this route does not know is refused, not promoted. A new lead shape is not a roster until somebody says it is.

_the_property: the evidence is the caption to a TEAM PHOTOGRAPH, not a photograph of something else
the club-season is one the archive HOLDS
_team_photograph_ruling._all_three_or_nothing: A caption alone is not enough. A man named in a photograph of something other than his club's team picture is not covered, and neither is a club-season the archive does not hold. The three conditions are checked as a property in promote_players.qualify() and again in src/gate_team_photograph_promotions.py; neither names a man.
_team_photograph_ruling._why: The twelve Pacific Coast Wildcats men failed not because they did not play but because PFA's box scores only see men who STARTED, and no source ever gave that club a roster. They were excluded by a gap in the evidence, not by evidence of absence. A man in uniform, in the team picture, named by the club's own opponent's programme, has a stronger claim to membership than most of what places men on 1920s clubs.
_team_photograph_ruling._the_predicate_does_not_move: `programme.team_photograph` is NOT roster membership and does not become it. The distinction survives the promotion: the man becomes a person, and the claim keeps saying exactly what it said -- that he was photographed with this club, not that he played. A promotion under this ruling must never write a roster_membership claim, and the gate checks that as its own property.
_team_photograph_ruling._what_is_still_refused: `boxscore_lineup`, `transaction` and `training_camp` are unchanged and still refused. Signed is not rostered; a camp list is who was invited; and a boxscore lead means the man did not resolve, which is an identity question, not a promotion.
